assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new quantum state of matter: a bulk insulator with protected boundary states set by band topology. It opened a field in which first-principles band structure (spin-orbit coupling, band inversion) and ARPES/transport measurements agree quantitatively, which is the kind of theory-experiment closure I value. Importance and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 quantum spin Hall idea; Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang predicted HgTe (not on the list); Molenkamp's group measured it in HgTe wells; Hasan's group established the 3D topological insulator experimentally by ARPES. Three names cannot cover all four credited people, so I would propose Kane (theory), Molenkamp (transport) and Hasan (3D materials), leaving Mele out; this is a real unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Predictions from 2005 and experiments from 2007 onward have been reproduced by many independent groups and by DFT calculations. The interpretation is stable and the field is mature; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Mele's omission is hard to justify since he co-authored the Z2 papers with Kane.
Predictions by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents 3D work are outside the credited names.
My knowledge of exact priority details is from memory and not independently checked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a theoretical flat-band prediction into a tunable platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity. It is a new quantum behaviour in a designed material, with a strong link to continuum-model and DFT-based theory. Impact on condensed matter is large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle (2011); Jarillo-Herrero's group measured correlated insulators and superconductivity (2018). Andrei's earlier STM evidence of flat bands and the Cao-Fatemi-Jarillo-Herrero first authors are an unresolved wrinkle; a theory-plus-experiment trio looks the fairest.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases, although sample-to-sample variation is large and the superconducting mechanism is still debated. Recognition is timely but the mechanism remains open.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not settled.
Andrei's and other groups' contributions complicate the attribution.
Reproducibility depends on twist-angle disorder.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DMFT is the central non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, and with DFT (DFT+DMFT) it gives quantitative predictions of spectra for Mott systems and correlated materials. The work is original, conceptually clear (the infinite-dimension limit) and has lasting impact. As a materials theorist I see its direct use in my own area.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping onto an impurity problem; Kotliar and collaborators extended it to real materials. Metzner is not on the credited list, so the trio of Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt is the best available fit within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: The method is decades old and thoroughly tested against photoemission and other spectroscopy; its limits (non-local correlations) are known. Recognition is mature, and the Nobel Committee has recognised few pure theory methods of this kind, which is a policy question not a scientific one.
uncertainties: Whether the committee will honour a computational method rather than a discovery.
Metzner's role is outside the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the giant effect in crystalline MgO barriers made magnetic tunnel junctions the basis of hard-disk read heads and MRAM. The physics (spin-dependent, symmetry-filtered tunnelling) is well explained by first-principles theory, so there is a clear physical discovery with major real use.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated the large MgO effect in 2004, following Butler and Mathon's theoretical prediction (not credited). Four people are credited for three slots; I would favour Moodera, Parkin and Yuasa but the choice relative to Miyazaki is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and commercially deployed for two decades, with strong independent confirmation. Timing is late but acceptable; a Nobel was already given for GMR in 2007, which raises questions about distinctiveness.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize.
Exclusion of Miyazaki and of theorists Butler and Mathon.
Parkin's priority in MgO versus Yuasa is contested in my memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MgB2 showed conventional two-gap superconductivity at 39 K, and the iron-based family opened a second class of high-temperature superconductors outside the cuprates. These discoveries are surprising, because many theorists did not expect it, and electronic structure calculations were crucial in discussing the multiband character.
assessment.attribution: Akimitsu discovered MgB2 (2001) and Hosono discovered superconductivity in LaFeAsO:F (2008); this pairing of two clear discoverers is straightforward. Each is credited with a different material family, so the candidate is a compound one that may not be a single discovery.
assessment.maturity: Both are confirmed by many groups. Multiband theory is robust for MgB2, but the pairing mechanism in iron-based superconductors is still unresolved, which weakens maturity.
uncertainties: Two distinct discoveries combined under one heading.
Pairing mechanism in the iron-based compounds is not settled.
High-Tc cuprates were already recognised in 1987, which affects novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fractional charge and anyonic exchange statistics are among the most surprising pieces of quantum behaviour in matter, and this would be recognition of a quantum-statistics discovery in two dimensions. Experiments have recently shown anyonic braiding signatures directly.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim predicted anyons in 1977; Heiblum's group measured fractional charge by shot noise; Manfra's ultra-clean GaAs samples and interferometers, and Fève's work on anyon collisions, supply the later evidence. Five names are credited, so a three-person selection leaves out important contributors; Laughlin's theory is already prized (1998).
assessment.maturity: Fractional charge is well confirmed; direct braiding statistics were seen only around 2020 to 2020s, and interpretations are still debated and need more independent confirmation.
uncertainties: Direct anyon-statistics evidence is still recent and partly contested.
Five credited names cannot be fitted into three slots.
The role of Fève versus Manfra in the decisive experiments is not clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters, with the Mott-insulator transition as the key demonstration. It gives a clean, quantitative way to study many-body physics relevant to correlated materials,. Impact is wide.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner, Bloch and Hänsch observed the Mott transition; Bloch's quantum gas microscope is a large step; Esslinger did the fermionic Mott insulator. Five names are credited, so any three is a partial answer; I would favour Bloch, Greiner and Zoller.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent groups and increasing use as quantum simulators; the Bose-Einstein condensation prize of 2001 and the 2012 and 2022 prizes in nearby areas lower the novelty somewhat.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier AMO prizes.
Jaksch and Hänsch are not in the credited list.
Whether the claim of useful quantum advantage over classical simulation is established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism is a newly identified class of collinear magnetic order, with zero net magnetisation and spin-split bands, that departs from the textbook division into ferro- and antiferromagnets. As a magnetism theorist I find it appealing and symmetry-based DFT work has been central; the possible spintronic consequences are significant.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth formulated the classification and its band-structure signatures in 2020 to 2022; other groups, including Hayami and Yuan, made earlier related proposals that are not in the credited list. The trio is coherent for the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation by ARPES and X-ray dichroism in MnTe and CrSb came only in 2024 and later; it is probably premature, and I would want more independent confirmation and tests of the device claims before it ranks higher.
uncertainties: Premature: confirmation is recent and the number of materials is small.
Priority claims by other researchers.
Device relevance remains speculative.
